summary: Kaniksu NF 50-ft pole L-6 tower, built about 1932 near Priest River, Idaho; destroyed in the 1960s; a 2022 trip report found no footings or other remains.

facts.design: 50-foot pole L-6 tower with ground log cabin living quarters
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1960s; a 2022 trip report found no footings, cable or trash pit at the site.

access.note: The road was gated in a 2022 trip report; the visitor parked at the gate and walked in.

visit.trail_note: No tower to climb. The 2022 trip report walked in along the road through a heavily logged area.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two sources give the cab as L-6 and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives L4. The story uses L-6, the design in the record and in two sources; the L4 claim is noted, not adopted.

notes_for_editor: The 1932 build date is 'about' or 'c.1932' on three sites; Rex's page attributes the date to Kresek, a source not checked. The L-6 vs L4 design disagrees and is flagged in the story. The 1936 road item is dated August 20, 1936 on Rex's page (a Newport Miner item as quoted there); the newspaper itself was not seen. The 1960s destruction has no year in any source, so no destroyed or removed event is dated. No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. The idahofirelookouts photo (jaspermtn1933, credit Fire Lookout Museum) has no stated licence and is not added. Access 'restricted' rests on the gated road in one 2022 trip report. Brief record matches: status gone, height 15.2 m (50 ft), design L-6, agency Kaniksu National Forest.
